geo.label: on hold / data-light
parts: Macro Stance

Services are holding up while hiring stalls: the January ISM services PMI printed 53.8% [[n7223]] and ADP counted just 22,000 private payrolls, far short of expectations [[n7232]]. The January jobs report is now due Feb. 11 after the shutdown delay [[n7230]], and Fed Governor Cook says inflation progress has stalled [[n7245]]. Solid activity, soft hiring and sticky inflation keep the Fed on hold, with the burden of proof on the labour data.
Rates & Curve

The 2Y held at 3.57% and the 10Y rose to 4.29%, widening the 10Y−2Y spread to 72 bps; over 20 observations the 2Y is up 10 bps and the 10Y 11 bps, a bear steepening with the curve moderately steep, approaching the long-run average (US Treasury, prior close 2026-02-04). Investors are ramping up bets on a steeper curve under a Warsh-led Fed [[n8022]]. The S&P 500 fell 0.5% to 6,882.72 and the VIX rose to 18.64, up 14.0% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-04).
New / Most Important

The AI selloff broadened — nearly $1 trillion has been wiped from software and services stocks as investors debate AI's existential threat [[n8061]] — but money is rotating, not leaving: AI anxiety is fuelling a comeback in value stocks [[n6022]]. The Dow rose 0.5% to 49,501.30 while the Nasdaq 100 fell 1.8% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-04): a rotation out of long-duration growth, not a macro risk-off.
Playbook ✓

Stay benchmark-weight with a value tilt (banks, energy, industrials) funded from software and second-tier AI hardware, and favour the 2Y over the 10Y while the spread holds at or above 72 bps (US Treasury, prior close 2026-02-04). Cut the steepener if the Feb. 11 payrolls print [[n7230]] validates ADP's weakness and the 2Y breaks below 3.47%, its level 20 observations ago.

geo.label: on hold / disinflation
parts: Macro Stance

Disinflation has arrived: euro-zone inflation fell to 1.7% in January [[n2682]], and European stocks still closed at a record high even as tech and healthcare dragged [[n2701]]. With growth holding and inflation below target, the ECB can stay on hold with an easing option in reserve — the best mix for European cyclicals and lenders.
Credit & Inflation

The risk sits in credit: the ECB's survey shows euro-zone banks tightening access to business credit [[n2626]], and the German 30-year yield has climbed to its highest since 2011 [[n2924]] — a term-premium story, not an inflation one, which keeps us short long duration even as policy rates stay put.
New / Most Important

The rotation into value is a European advantage: chemical stocks surged on optimism over emission rules [[n2703]], the CAC 40 rose 1.0% to 8,262.16 and the FTSE 100 0.9% to 10,402.30, while the tech-heavier DAX fell 0.7% to 24,603.04 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-04). EUR/USD edged up 0.2% to 1.1816 but is down 1.7% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-04).
Playbook ✓

Overweight euro-area banks, chemicals and energy; underweight software and information services. Keep long-dated Bund exposure light while the 30-year sits at post-2011 highs [[n2924]]. Change the call if tighter lending [[n2626]] shows up in PMIs, which would turn disinflation from a gift into a growth warning.

geo.label: easing bias / weak domestic demand
parts: Macro Stance

China remains a two-speed economy: exporters and high-tech manufacturing carry growth while households, property and local finances weaken. China logged its first fiscal revenue drop since 2020 on the property slump and weak consumption [[n0785]], and Beijing is now raising taxes on select sectors [[n1051]] — a sign it is rationing fiscal support rather than expanding it. We stay bearish on domestic demand and selective on exporters.
PMIs & Activity

The January official manufacturing PMI fell to 49.3 [[n0783]], while the private survey showed factory activity growing at its fastest pace since October and beating the official reading [[n0855]]. The split favours private and export-oriented firms over the state-heavy domestic sector. No newer official print is available, so the next official PMI is the confirmation test.
Credit Impulse

The latest credit print (December) was weak: 2025 new bank loans were the lowest in seven years, and Reuters notes policy support is needed [[n0513]]. Lower funding costs have not created borrowers, so we read the credit impulse as still negative until household lending turns. A January credit print with rising household loans would change the call; the feed carries none yet.
Property

Property is still the drag: sales declines accelerated in a 'bleak start' to 2026 for the sector [[n7164]]. Policy has shifted to supporting developer funding and prices rather than demand, which leaves property-linked lenders and building materials as funding sources, not holdings. A stabilisation in new-home sales is the signal to revisit.
Fiscal, Policy & Trade

Fiscal room is shrinking: the revenue drop [[n0785]] and the tax increases on select sectors [[n1051]] point to a government raising revenue rather than spending its way out. Exports remain the growth engine, which makes the currency and exporters' margins the policy variables to watch. A managed yuan appreciation would squeeze exactly the sector carrying growth.
Markets & Flows

The Shanghai Composite rose 0.9% to 4,102.20, up 0.4% over 20 sessions, and the Hang Seng was flat at 26,847.32 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-04). Hong Kong-listed Chinese tech entered a bear market as tax and AI fears took hold [[n1088]]: KWEB fell 2.9% to 33.42 and is down 8.0% over 20 sessions, and FXI is down 5.5% over five sessions, while ASHR rose 0.7% to 33.48 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-04). USD/CNY eased to 6.9377, a 0.65% yuan gain over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-04).
New / Most Important

Two policy signals dominate: Beijing is raising taxes on select sectors [[n1051]], and the tax-and-AI scare has pushed Hong Kong-listed tech into a bear market [[n1088]]. Onshore A-shares are holding up while offshore internet names break down — the market is pricing domestic liquidity support for the mainland and regulatory risk for the platforms.
Playbook ✓

Prefer onshore A-shares (ASHR) over Hong Kong internet (KWEB) until the tax picture clears; avoid developers and property-linked lenders. Add China cyclicals only on a January credit print with rising household loans [[n0513]] or an official PMI back above 50. ⚠ Divergence: the private manufacturing PMI's fastest growth since October [[n0855]] says activity is firmer than the official 49.3 suggests [[n0783]].

geo.label: pro-growth vote / BOJ restraint
parts: Macro Stance

Japan heads into its election with the dollar firming and the yen under pressure [[n8112]], and a Reuters exclusive says the BOJ won't come to the rescue of a Takaichi-driven bond rout [[n3556]]. Fiscal expansion without a central-bank backstop is bullish for domestic earners and banks, and bearish for long-dated JGBs.
Activity & Currency

The Nikkei 225 slipped 0.8% to 54,293.36 but is up 3.4% over 20 sessions, and USD/JPY rose 0.2% to 155.80, up 2.2% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-04). MUFG's profit rose as BOJ rate increases bolstered lending income [[n3558]], the clearest evidence that normalisation is feeding bank earnings.
Playbook ✓

Own Japanese banks and domestic cyclicals, currency-hedged; avoid long-dated JGBs and keep a small long-yen option against intervention. Change the call if a weak election result removes the fiscal impulse, or if a disorderly JGB sell-off forces the BOJ to reverse its stance [[n3556]].

geo.label: hiking / overheating
parts: Macro Stance

The RBA's 25bps hike to 3.85% [[n0195]] is unlikely to be the last: the WSJ says Australia's overheating economy signals more rate pain ahead [[n0317]]. Domestic demand and housing will carry the adjustment while the central bank re-establishes credibility.
Demand & Financing

AUD/USD climbed 1.0% to 0.7023 and is up 4.2% over 20 sessions, while the ASX 200 rose 0.8% to 8,927.80 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-04). A stronger currency tightens conditions on top of the hike, adding to the squeeze on mortgage holders and import-competing firms.
Playbook ✓

Underweight rate-sensitive domestic cyclicals and REITs; prefer the major banks and keep the long-AUD position, now at 0.7023 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-04). Reverse if monthly CPI rolls over or unemployment rises, which would end the case for more rate pain [[n0317]].

geo.label: on hold / strong growth
parts: Monetary & Activity

The MPC kept rates unchanged, with experts split until the last minute (Polish: 'RPP utrzymała stopy procentowe. Eksperci byli podzieleni do ostatniej chwili') [[n4287]], and StockWatch reads the council as waiting for March ('RPP czeka na marzec') [[n4290]]. The pause comes against GDP growth of 3.6% in 2025 [[n3660]], so the hold is a choice, not a constraint: easing is paused, not over.
FX & Markets

Warsaw set a historic record twice in one session (Polish: 'Historyczny rekord na giełdzie w Warszawie. Dwa razy w ciągu jednego dnia') [[n4310]]. The WIG20TR ETF rose 0.7% to 68.83 while EPOL slipped 0.2% to 38.28; EUR/PLN was unchanged at 4.2196 and USD/PLN eased 0.15% to 3.5714 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-04). Orlen rose 4.2% to 110.52 and Dino 4.8% to 39.81, while KGHM fell 1.8% to 333.90 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-04).
Companies

Polish IT is losing billions even as the WIG hits records ('Dlaczego polskie IT traci miliardy?') [[n4314]]: CD Projekt is down 11.8% over five sessions to 251.90 and Allegro 11.9% over 20 sessions to 28.90, while Pekao is up 7.9% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-04). Leadership sits with banks, energy and discount retail; the laggards are names exposed to AI disruption or platform competition.
Security & New Development

Drone maker WB Electronics is eyeing a Warsaw IPO around the turn of the year [[n3708]], which would give investors a listed play on Poland's defence build-out and deepen a market that still leans on banks, energy and KGHM.
Playbook ✓

Stay overweight Poland via the WIG20TR ETF and EPOL with banks (PKO BP, Pekao) and Orlen as the core; the hold protects bank margins. Underweight Polish IT and gaming until the AI-disruption repricing [[n4314]] stabilises. Re-assess if the March meeting [[n4290]] delivers a cut alongside weaker activity. ⚠ Divergence: the WIG's records [[n4310]] came on a day the dollar-based EPOL fell while the local WIG20TR tracker rose — the foreign vehicle is lagging the local tape.
Narrative

The software rout deepened: nearly $1 trillion has been wiped from software and services stocks [[n8061]], and hedge funds have made $24 billion shorting software so far in 2026 and are increasing the bet [[n6020]]. XLK fell 2.8% and is down 7.4% over five sessions, with Oracle down 24.3% and Palantir 22.35% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-04).
Reported

Super Micro raised its annual revenue forecast on strong demand for its servers [[n2136]], a hardware beat that contrasts with the software tape. Palantir fell 11.6% to 139.54 in the prior session, while Apple rose 2.6% to 276.49 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-04).
EPS Upside Watch

Hardware with physical AI demand still earns upgrades — Super Micro's raised outlook [[n2136]] and Apple's 7.8% five-session gain (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-04) — and Microsoft, down 14.0% over five sessions, rose 0.7% as the first megacap to stabilise (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-04).
⚡ Breaking Convention

Positioning is now the contrarian signal: hedge funds are adding to software shorts that have already paid $24 billion [[n6020]], so the trade is crowded on the short side. A single strong software guide could trigger a violent squeeze — keep shorts in per-seat SaaS small and hedged.
Narrative

Alphabet reset the bar for AI spending: it said 2026 capital spending could double as its cloud business booms [[n5993]], and the capex plan spooked investors [[n5995]]. XLC fell 0.8% and Meta 3.3% in the prior session, with GOOGL down 2.0% to 333.04 before the report (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-04).
Reported

Snap rose on fourth-quarter sales that beat [[n2243]], a sign that ad platforms with better targeting are still being paid. Alphabet beat as well, but the debate has moved from revenue to the return on a doubled capex budget [[n5993]].
EPS Upside Watch

Snap's beat [[n2243]] says ad budgets are healthy, which supports Meta after its 3.3% slide. Netflix, down 11.6% over 20 sessions at 80.16 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-04), already prices much of its estimate risk.
⚡ Breaking Convention

A capex increase that once would have been cheered now spooks investors [[n5995]]: the market wants proof of return before it pays for spend. That flips the AI trade from buying the spenders to buying their suppliers, as Broadcom's and Nvidia's gains on Google's capex showed [[n5973]].
Narrative

Banks are the main winners of the value rotation: XLF rose 0.8% and Bank of America 1.7%, up 6.9% over five sessions, and JPMorgan is up 5.5% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-04). A steeper curve and steady capital rules — the Fed opted to keep bank capital buffers steady until 2027 [[n8021]] — support net interest income and buybacks.
Reported

UBS beat with a $1.2 billion fourth-quarter profit and plans a $3 billion buyback [[n2254]] — European lenders are converting excess capital into payouts. Goldman Sachs fell 2.7% to 913.30 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-04) as capital-markets franchises lag deposit-funded lenders.
EPS Upside Watch

European lenders are near a re-rating milestone: BNP Paribas and SocGen eye a long-awaited break above book value [[n6053]]. In the US, deposit-rich money-centre banks have the cleanest estimate upside from a 10Y−2Y spread at 72 bps (US Treasury, prior close 2026-02-04).
⚡ Breaking Convention

Private credit, once the hottest bet on Wall Street, has started to crack [[n6057]] — the rotation lifting banks is draining the alternative managers. Long banks against BDCs and alternative managers is the cleanest expression.
Narrative

Oil's geopolitical bid is building: Brent rose 3.2% to $69.46 and is up 14.4% over 20 sessions, while XLE is up 15.8% and Exxon 21.9% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-04). Oil climbed 3% as the market awaited US-Iran talks [[n6029]].
Reported

European majors are retreating on shareholder returns: Equinor cut buybacks by 70% and flagged a sharp drop in capital expenditure [[n2283]]. US majors are the opposite story, with Chevron up 15.8% over 20 sessions to 181.23 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-04).
EPS Upside Watch

US integrated majors with low-cost growth barrels gain most from a higher Brent, and gas-weighted producers get a second lever: Henry Hub rose 4.65% to $3.46 after a 53.55% five-session collapse (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-04).
⚡ Breaking Convention

Equinor's 70% buyback cut [[n2283]] warns that European majors are prioritising balance sheets over payouts even as Brent rises. The US-Europe split in capital returns argues for owning XOM and CVX over the European majors.
Narrative

Industrials hold the AI-capex bid without the disruption risk: XLI rose 0.3% and is up 4.55% over 20 sessions, with Caterpillar up 11.0% over 20 sessions despite a 1.6% dip (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-04). The TVA is pursuing 6.2 GW of new generation, citing data centres and population growth [[n6104]].
Reported

Johnson Controls reported strong first-quarter results and raised FY26 guidance [[n2224]], while Daikin slid the most in 18 months after cutting its profit outlook [[n2229]]. Building-controls and data-centre exposure is the differentiator.
EPS Upside Watch

Power-generation and grid suppliers: utility build plans like TVA's 6.2 GW [[n6104]] translate into multi-year orders for turbines, transformers and switchgear. GE closed at 308.34, up 5.4% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-04).
⚡ Breaking Convention

Daikin's outlook cut [[n2229]] shows not every 'data-centre' industrial wins: commoditised HVAC faces margin pressure while specialised controls such as Johnson Controls [[n2224]] gain. Be selective within the AI-capex basket rather than owning it wholesale.
Narrative

Discretionary keeps lagging: XLY fell 0.7% and is down 0.8% over 20 sessions, with Tesla down 3.8% and Amazon 2.4% in the prior session (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-04). The value rotation is not reaching names exposed to a stretched middle-income shopper.
Reported

Uber fell on an earnings and guidance miss [[n2219]], a reminder that even platform leaders are judged on profit guidance rather than growth. Nike rose 5.4% to 64.22 and Home Depot 1.6% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-04) as beaten-down names drew value buyers.
EPS Upside Watch

Amazon reports Thursday, with options pricing a large post-earnings move [[n2146]]; after Alphabet's capex shock, the swing factor is whether AWS growth justifies the spend. AMZN is down 4.1% over five sessions at 232.99 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-04).
⚡ Breaking Convention

The rotation is lifting the most-hated discretionary names (Nike) rather than quality compounders, so part of the move is short-covering, not fundamentals. Fade those squeezes unless guidance improves.
Narrative

Staples keep absorbing defensive money: XLP rose 1.3% and is up 12.3% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-04), and Berkshire is shining as investors go defensive [[n6181]]. Walmart closed at 128.00, up 9.8% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-04).
Reported

E.l.f. Beauty beat and raised full-year guidance [[n2223]], evidence that value-priced brands are winning share in a trading-down economy. Costco was flat at 978.35 and is up 10.0% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-04).
EPS Upside Watch

Value-priced personal care and scale grocers: E.l.f.'s guidance raise [[n2223]] and Walmart's momentum point to share gains for low-price formats. Estimates for these names can rise even while branded packaged food competes on price.
⚡ Breaking Convention

Staples are now a crowded momentum trade: a 12.3% 20-session gain for XLP (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-04) and defensive buying of Berkshire [[n6181]] mean the sector's protection is already priced. Own the share-gainers and avoid adding to the broad sector at these levels.
Narrative

Healthcare is a stock-picker's sector: Lilly jumped 10.3% to 1,107.12 while UnitedHealth fell 2.9% and is down 20.9% over 20 sessions, and XLV rose 1.25% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-04). Novo Nordisk sank 17% after its bleak 2026 forecast [[n2249]].
Reported

Lilly expects its sales surge to continue in 2026 even with pricing headwinds [[n2258]], while Boston Scientific beat but was the worst stock in the S&P 500 [[n2211]]. Beats are not enough; the 2026 guide decides the reaction.
EPS Upside Watch

Lilly remains the estimate-revision leader because volume growth is outrunning price cuts [[n2258]], the opposite of Novo's guide [[n2249]]. Devices and tools with cautious guides are where 2026 numbers still need to come down.
⚡ Breaking Convention

The obesity price war is producing a winner, not a casualty: the same pricing pressure sank Novo 17% [[n2249]] while Lilly rose 10.3% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-04). Long Lilly against Novo is the cleanest expression; shorting the theme is the wrong trade.
Narrative

Materials outperformed in the rotation: XLB rose 2.35% and is up 9.2% over 20 sessions, while gold closed at $4,950.80, up 10.1% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-04). Gold firming while copper falls shows the precious-metals bid is geopolitical, not cyclical.
Reported

Anglo American reported a 10% drop in 2025 copper output and cut its 2026 guidance [[n2227]]. Copper still fell 3.9% to $5.83/lb and Freeport 4.35% in the prior session (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-04).
EPS Upside Watch

European chemicals have a fresh catalyst after surging on emission-rules optimism [[n2703]], a policy tailwind for energy-intensive producers. Copper producers with growing output gain from Anglo's guidance cut [[n2227]] — lost supply at one miner is pricing power for the rest.
⚡ Breaking Convention

Copper is falling while chemicals and gold rally: the AI data-centre and grid metal is consolidating after its run, down 3.1% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-04). Use the pullback to add copper producers rather than chase gold miners.
Narrative
Real estate is catching rotation money: XLRE rose 1.6% and is up 1.9% over 20 sessions, even as the 10Y edged up to 4.29% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-04; US Treasury, prior close 2026-02-04).
Reported
Crown Castle dipped after soft EBITDA guidance and announced job cuts [[n2228]] — tower REITs face the same 'guide decides' rule as the rest of the market.
EPS Upside Watch

Data-centre and healthcare landlords remain the estimate-upgrade candidates as AI build-outs absorb powered capacity; towers and residential have the least visibility. The 10Y at 4.29%, up 11 bps over 20 observations (US Treasury, prior close 2026-02-04), caps multiple expansion.
⚡ Breaking Convention

REITs rallied on a day long yields rose, so the move is rotation money, not a rates call: if the 30Y at 4.91% (US Treasury, prior close 2026-02-04) keeps climbing, the bounce fades. Use strength to trim towers and residential.
Narrative

Utilities are splitting in two: NextEra rose 1.3% and is up 11.0% over 20 sessions, while Constellation fell 6.7% and is down 29.4% over 20 sessions and Vistra fell 6.85% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-04). XLU slipped 0.4% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-04).
Reported

Spire's profit jumped as rate increases lifted gas-utility earnings [[n2307]] — regulated rate relief is turning into EPS. No merchant-generator result in the feed explains Constellation's slide; the move reads as de-risking of AI-power beta.
EPS Upside Watch
Regulated utilities with rate cases and data-centre load growth, such as NextEra, have the most visible upside; the TVA's 6.2 GW plan [[n6104]] shows how much new generation the grid needs.
⚡ Breaking Convention

Josh Shapiro is leaning on the tech industry to bear energy costs [[n6110]], adding to pressure over who pays for data-centre power. Cost allocation to hyperscalers protects regulated utilities but caps merchant generators' upside — hence the split; own NEE-type regulated names over CEG and VST.
Narrative

European autos ripped higher in the value rotation: the SXAP tracker rose 3.7%, with Renault up 5.2%, Mercedes 4.1%, BMW 3.9% and Volkswagen 3.7% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-04). Stellantis and VW are dialling up pressure on the EU to defend the auto industry [[n6062]], raising the odds of regulatory relief.
Reported

No major European carmaker reported in the window. Stellantis faces Peugeot model delays from battery-plant snags [[n6086]], a reminder that execution risk remains even as the stock rose 3.1% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-04).
EPS Upside Watch

Volkswagen has the momentum: its preference shares are up 3.7% over 20 sessions, and Mercedes 1.0%, the only majors positive over that span (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-04). Regulatory relief from Brussels [[n6062]] would help the volume makers most.
⚡ Breaking Convention

A one-day rally on rotation and lobbying does not fix Chinese competition or battery execution [[n6086]]; the SXAP tracker is still down 0.2% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-04). Use strength to rotate from Stellantis and Renault into VW and Mercedes rather than add to the sector.
Narrative

Semis sold off hard, but the demand signal got stronger: Alphabet's surging capex lifted Broadcom and Nvidia [[n5973]]. SOXX fell 4.4% and is down 8.3% over five sessions, with AMD down 17.3%, Micron 9.55% and ASML 4.1% in the prior session (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-04).
Reported

AMD suffered its worst rout since 2018 on a disappointing forecast [[n2273]]. Qualcomm sank as the memory shortage dragged on its forecast [[n2300]], and Arm fell as licensing sales missed [[n2217]] — handset-exposed chips are the casualties of the memory squeeze.
EPS Upside Watch

Custom-silicon and networking suppliers to the hyperscalers: Alphabet plans to double capex to a possible $185 billion [[n5994]], which flows directly to Broadcom, down 10.4% over 20 sessions to 308.05 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-04). TSM at 325.74 is the leading-edge foundry beneficiary (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-04).
⚡ Breaking Convention

The memory shortage that powers memory pricing is now destroying demand elsewhere — Qualcomm's forecast [[n2300]] shows smartphones absorbing the cost. Inside semis it is a zero-sum trade: own AI-infrastructure chips and avoid handset chips.

earnings_pattern.title: Guides and capex returns decide the tape
parts: Rewarded

Lilly jumped 10.3% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-04) on a guide that expects its sales surge to continue [[n2258]], Super Micro raised its revenue forecast [[n2136]], Snap rose on a sales beat [[n2243]], and E.l.f. Beauty beat and raised guidance [[n2223]].
Punished

AMD suffered its worst rout since 2018 [[n2273]], Novo sank 17% on a bleak forecast [[n2249]], Boston Scientific was the S&P 500's worst stock despite a beat [[n2211]], and Uber fell on a guidance miss [[n2219]]. Alphabet's beat came with a capex plan that spooked investors [[n5995]].
Pattern

The common thread is guidance and cost exposure: beats with cautious guides are sold, and the memory shortage splits winners from losers — Super Micro's servers against Qualcomm's handsets [[n2300]]. Capex raises are no longer rewarded on their own; investors want evidence of return before paying for spend.
Attention into EPS

Amazon reports Thursday [[n2146]], and MarketWatch says its most important figure comes with a high bar [[n2269]]. After Alphabet's reception, AWS growth relative to the capex plan decides whether the hyperscaler trade takes a second leg down.
Playbook

Own guide-raisers on pullbacks (Lilly, hardware with visible AI demand) and sell beats with cautious guides into strength. Into Amazon, hedge long exposure with puts rather than adding. Change the call if Amazon raises capex and is rewarded, which would signal the market is again willing to pay for AI spend.

underowned.title: Quality software after the 'SaaSpocalypse'
parts: Attention Gap

JPMorgan says software stocks are now 'sentenced before trial' [[n6008]], and hedge funds have made $24 billion shorting the group and are increasing the bet [[n6020]]. With the short side this crowded and long-only buyers absent, the asymmetry is shifting toward platforms with pricing power and AI-native products.
Exposure & Risk

Build positions slowly in diversified software (IGV) or quality platforms such as Microsoft, down 13.4% over 20 sessions to 414.19 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-04), hedged with index puts. Risk: AI substitution is real for seat-based tools, so avoid per-seat application vendors and wait for one guidance cycle before sizing up.

underowned.title: Japanese banks into BOJ normalisation
parts: Attention Gap

MUFG's profit rose as BOJ rate increases bolstered lending income [[n3558]], yet global attention on Japan is fixed on the yen and the election. With the BOJ signalling it won't backstop a fiscal-driven bond rout [[n3556]], higher JGB yields are an earnings tailwind for lenders that few global portfolios hold directly.
Exposure & Risk

Express via MUFG, SMFG or a currency-hedged Japan financials basket. Risk: a disorderly bond sell-off creates mark-to-market losses on securities books, so prefer lenders with short-duration holdings and avoid life insurers with large long-bond portfolios.

crypto.title: Bitcoin trades like a software stock — and that is the problem
parts: Market Context

Bitcoin's prior completed daily close was $73,019.70, down 3.5% on the day, 13.2% over five sessions and 23.6% over 20 sessions; ether closed at $2,143.50 and solana at $92.03, down 35.4% and 35.3% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-04). IBIT fell 4.0% to 41.57 and Coinbase 6.1%, leaving Coinbase down 32.7% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-04). Bitcoin bled for a second straight day and nearly grazed $72,000 [[n1348]].
New / Most Important

The selling is institutional: spot bitcoin ETF outflows total $2.9B as the price hits a new 2026 low [[n1361]], and MSTR fell 3.1% to 129.09, down 18.5% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-04). CoinDesk's read that bitcoin 'might just be another software name' [[n1349]] captures the problem — crypto is trading as long-duration tech beta in an AI-disruption selloff, not as a hedge.
Playbook

Bearish. Stay out until ETF outflows reverse; the $72,000 area tested in the latest leg [[n1348]] is the line, and a daily close below it opens a deeper flush. Prefer IBIT over Strategy and other leveraged proxies, and hedge any exposure with puts. Turn constructive only on stabilising flows or a legislative compromise that unlocks stablecoin growth.

flows.title: Steepener bets, a firmer dollar and the value rotation
parts: Rates & Dollar

DXY rose 0.2% to 97.62 and is up 1.2% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-04), but a Reuters poll says the dollar's rebound will be cut short by rate-cut bets and doubts over Fed independence [[n8025]]. The 10Y−2Y spread widened to 72 bps with the 30Y at 4.91%, and the curve is moderately steep, approaching the long-run average (US Treasury, prior close 2026-02-04). TLT fell 0.25% and IEF was flat (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-04).
Credit Check

Credit is calm on the surface — HYG slipped 0.1% and LQD 0.1% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-04) — but private credit, once Wall Street's hottest bet, has started to crack [[n6057]]. The gap between stable public spreads and stress in private software loans is the risk to watch.
Portfolio Implication

Run a curve steepener (long 2Y against 10Y–30Y duration) while investors ramp up steeper-curve bets under Warsh [[n8022]], keep a value tilt in equities, and hold IG over HY. Reverse the steepener if the Feb. 11 payrolls print [[n7230]] is weak enough to revive near-term cuts and the 2Y falls below 3.47%.

anticipatory.title: US-Iran talks in Oman: the oil premium
parts: What Is Priced

US-Iran nuclear talks are set for Oman [[n3255]], and oil rose after Trump said Iran's supreme leader 'should be very worried' [[n6033]]. Brent at $69.46 is up 14.4% over 20 sessions and WTI at $65.14 is up 14.0% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-04) — a rising geopolitical premium.
Conditional Expression

If talks open constructively, the premium deflates fast: own refiners and airlines and overwrite upstream positions. If talks stall or incidents escalate, own XLE and Brent call spreads; the oil-equity hedge remains cheaper than outright crude.
Risk
Incidents at sea or in the air can override diplomacy at any moment, so keep sizes small and use options rather than futures; a de-escalation surprise would erase the 20-session gain quickly.

anticipatory.title: Japan's election: fiscal push without a BOJ backstop
parts: What Is Priced

Markets are positioned for a strong Takaichi mandate: the dollar firmed and the yen came under pressure ahead of the vote [[n8112]], with USD/JPY up 2.2% over five sessions to 155.80 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-04).
Conditional Expression

A landslide favours Japanese banks, domestic cyclicals and a weaker yen: express via hedged Japan equities and short long-dated JGBs. A disappointing result would reverse the yen trade quickly, so yen calls are the cheap hedge.
Risk
The BOJ won't rescue a Takaichi-driven bond rout [[n3556]], so a fiscal splurge could push JGB yields high enough to hit equities and force intervention; size the short-JGB leg conservatively.

catalysts.title: $AVGO — the supplier behind Google's doubled capex
parts: Catalyst & Thesis

Alphabet plans to double capex to a possible $185 billion [[n5994]], and Broadcom shares rose on the surging Google spending [[n5973]]. Thesis: in a market that now doubts the spenders, the suppliers of custom AI silicon are the direct beneficiaries.
Price Hurdle & Risk

AVGO closed at 308.05, down 3.8% in the prior session and 10.4% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-04), so the entry already discounts the AI selloff. Risk: if investors punish hyperscaler capex hard enough to force cuts, supplier orders follow; exit on any capex retrenchment signal.

catalysts.title: $AMZN — capex test on Thursday
parts: Catalyst & Thesis

Amazon reports Thursday [[n2146]], and MarketWatch says its most important figure comes with a high bar [[n2269]]. Thesis: after Alphabet's capex plan spooked investors [[n5995]], a large Amazon capex increase without a matching AWS acceleration is more likely to be sold than bought.
Price Hurdle & Risk

AMZN closed at 232.99, down 4.1% over five sessions and 3.3% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-04). Risk: a strong AWS acceleration would squeeze shorts, so express the view with put spreads rather than outright shorts.

catalysts.title: $LLY — the obesity price war's winner
parts: Catalyst & Thesis

Lilly's fourth-quarter report showed Mounjaro and Zepbound pushing revenue up 46% [[n2291]], and the company expects its sales surge to continue in 2026 despite pricing headwinds [[n2258]]. Thesis: volume growth is outrunning price cuts, the mirror image of Novo's guide.
Price Hurdle & Risk

LLY closed at 1,107.12 after a 10.3% jump and is up 4.05% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-04). Risk: after a double-digit gap, pullbacks are likely; add on weakness rather than chase, and cut if new US pricing rules start to hit volumes.

retail.title: Figma / FIG — retail buys the software crash
parts: Observed Attention
Stocktwits reports Figma is down over 40% this year and retail traders feel it's a steal [[n4530]]. That dip-buying runs into a sector where nearly $1 trillion of value has been wiped out [[n8061]].
Motivation & Bias
Anchoring on earlier prices and the belief that design software is AI-proof; the bias is treating a lower price as a margin of safety while the market re-rates the whole category.
Instrument & Risk
Shares only and small size; avoid short-dated calls in a sector where hedge funds are adding to shorts [[n6020]]. A squeeze is possible, but a guide confirming AI pressure would extend the drawdown.

retail.title: GameStop / GME — Burry's bet revives the meme
parts: Observed Attention
24/7 Wall St. reports Michael Burry is betting GameStop will 'level up' [[n4507]], reviving attention on the original meme stock while megacap tech sells off.
Motivation & Bias
Authority bias and nostalgia: a famous contrarian's position lends credibility, and the meme playbook offers a lottery-ticket payoff when the index leaders are falling.
Instrument & Risk

GME options carry very high implied volatility; if participating, use defined-risk spreads and keep size small. The investment case is separate from the meme, and momentum can reverse as fast as it builds.

retail.title: BitMine / BMNR — Ark keeps buying the ether proxy
parts: Observed Attention

Yahoo Finance asks why Cathie Wood is buying more BitMine as ether plummets, with Tom Lee defending the strategy [[n1358]]. Ether closed at $2,143.50, down 20.7% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-04).
Motivation & Bias
Following a high-profile buyer (authority bias) and averaging down into a falling asset (sunk-cost anchoring).
Instrument & Risk
BMNR is a leveraged ether proxy; with spot bitcoin ETFs bleeding $2.9B [[n1361]], crypto-treasury premiums can compress further. Prefer spot ETFs and hedge any proxy position with puts.

retail.title: SpaceX IPO / index fast entry — the access trade
parts: Observed Attention
SpaceX is seeking early index entry as it prepares a massive IPO [[n8079]], turning a private company into a retail talking point well before any listing.
Motivation & Bias
Retail treats index inclusion as guaranteed demand; the bias is assuming forced passive buying can only push prices up.
Instrument & Risk

Until a listing exists, proxies carry premiums that can collapse on timing news. If early index entry is granted, index funds would need to sell other holdings to make room — a hidden cost for existing megacap holders.
